title: Classes and prototypes
learningObjectives: Explain classes and prototypes and debug or organise JavaScript code using the concept.

understand.concept: JavaScript objects use prototypes for property and method lookup. Classes provide syntax for creating constructor functions and prototype methods, including inheritance with extends and super. JavaScript remains prototype-based underneath the class syntax.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding prototypes explains method sharing and inheritance behaviour. Classes are useful for some models but do not replace simpler objects and functions when those are clearer.
understand.analogy: A class is a convenient blueprint syntax; prototype lookup is the mechanism that helps objects share behaviour.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; debugger, module, prototype, and function-call behaviour follow JavaScript and browser runtime rules.

explain.narrative: The class constructor creates an instance, and describe is available through the class prototype.

examples.explanation: The class constructor creates an instance, and describe is available through the class prototype.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console or page demonstrates the code organisation or runtime behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Create a Course class with a constructor and method. Inspect Object.getPrototypeOf(instance) and explain where the method is found.
practise.independentTask: Create a small example that uses the feature. Inspect its runtime behaviour and explain the scope, receiver, or call path involved.
hints: Use breakpoints to inspect changing values.
Test methods both through their object and when passed as callbacks.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Classes and prototypes</title></head><body>
<script>class Course{constructor(title){this.title=title;}describe(){return `Course: ${this.title}`;}}const html=new Course('HTML');console.log(html.describe());</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Where are class instance methods typically stored?
questions.explanation: Class methods are defined on the prototype object shared by instances.

questions.prompt: What is a useful debugging or architecture practice?
options: Inspect actual runtime behaviour and keep dependencies explicit
Assume the code behaves as intended
questions.answer: Inspect actual runtime behaviour and keep dependencies explicit
questions.explanation: Reliable debugging and modular design depend on understanding actual execution and dependencies.
